stories.title: CFL players invited to Canadian flag football camp
stories.summary: Tyrell Ford and Tyson Philpot won't have much down time after playing in the Grey Cup game Sunday.

stories.title: Shaping Saskatchewan: Naomi Lendvay
stories.summary: At just six years old, Naomi Lendvay was diagnosed with Rhabdomyosarcoma and was told she had just 12 months to live. Unexpectedly, a testing drug ended up killing her cancer.

stories.title: ‘Intent is to try to appeal’ encampment cleanup order, Saskatoon organization says
stories.summary: Station 20 West says it received a notice to remove the encampment in front of its 20th Street facility from the City of Saskatoon but will not comply until the two parties meet.

stories.title: Saskatchewan hospital safety review complete, but findings won’t be released yet
stories.summary: The six-month review is now in the health ministry's hands, but Health Minister Jeremy Cockrill says he does not want to expose vulnerabilities until they are addressed.

stories.title: Marital hiss: Cat rescue raises more than $30K with donation to annoy ex-husband
stories.summary: A cat rescue in Saskatoon has started a fundraising campaign that involved some post-marital pettiness, but no one thought the $10,000 goal would be raised in less than 72 hours.

stories.title: Elks kicker Blanchard wrote it down in 2026
stories.summary: Vincent Blanchard began writing things down this season.

stories.title: Saskatoon police officer who was hit by vehicle stable, still in hospital
stories.summary: The Saskatoon police officer who was stuck by a vehicle on Wednesday afternoon is still undergoing treatment in hospital, but is now stable, SPS Chief Cameron McBride said.

stories.title: Man charged with second-degree murder for April death in Saskatoon
stories.summary: A 38-year-old man is facing a second-degree murder charge in relation to the death of Wray Musqua, who was found unresponsive by Saskatoon police officers in April.

stories.title: Woman found safe after alleged car theft near Prince Albert: RCMP
stories.summary: Shaylynn Ermine, 29, is described by Saskatchewan RCMP as five-feet, four-inches tall and 130 lbs., with brown eyes and black, shoulder-length hair.

stories.title: Is your relative honoured with a Geo-Memorial?
stories.summary: The project highlights a provincial tradition that began in 1947, when Saskatchewan started naming geographical features after its war dead.
